parent_comment: I've done a lot of photography, including a lot of B&W negative/darkroom printing. I was all set to wine and gripe about colorizing old B&W photos. But I realized that I've spent a lot of time training by brain to visualize what the B&W photo of a real scene will look like, and conversely how reality looked when looking at a B&W print. I realized that for lots of people, they haven't had the experiences to build up that "reverse engineering", and for them, decent colorization helps to make these images go from strange and unfamiliar to much more direct, real and understandable. So, I'll skip the rant. A lot of these are "snapshots" so it's not like destroying a great work of art (eg colorizing great B&W images from the likes of Ansel Adams or Henri Cartier-Bresson) (that said, in quite a few of the images I find the colorizing a bit clumsy and distracting... oh well.)
neutral_comment: I appreciate your perspective on colorizing old B&W photos. It's interesting to consider how experience shapes our understanding of these images. I've spent a lot of time developing the ability to visualize scenes in B&W and interpret B&W prints, and I recognize that not everyone has that same background. For those who haven't had that training, colorization can make these images more accessible and relatable. While I sometimes find the colorization choices a bit distracting, I understand its potential value.

It's problematic that the system currently legitimizes low turnout as acceptable, and it would be beneficial to consider requiring a minimum participation level, like a quorum, for elections to be valid. He had some interesting points that I wrote down - It is morally acceptable to use force to take someone else's money, and he would be ok with holding a gun to my head to make me pay for someone else's children - If there is no government, the poor will starve - Libertarians are just greedy Republicans - If you give money up under threat of force without putting up a fight, you're consenting - Society could not function without government - If someone has a million dollars, and you take all but a penny, that's taxation.
